Equations can contain more than one variable. For example, the following equation has two variables, [MATH: \color{blue}x] and [MATH: {\color{red}y}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}x} - 7{\color{red}y} = 1]

Content:
To solve the equation for the variable [MATH: {\color{blue}{x}},] we need to isolate [MATH: \color{blue}x] on one side of the equation:

Content:
In this case, we apply the addition principle and add [MATH: 7{\color{red}y}] to both sides:

Content:
[MATH: x − 7y|= 1; x − 7y + 7y|= 1 + 7y; x + 0|= 1 + 7y; x|= 1 + 7y]

Content:
And that's it! We have successfully isolated the variable [MATH: {\color{blue}{x}}.]

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 12\mathbin{:}]
